comparator.name: BSc Economics and Business Economics — Economics profile
comparator.sourceNotes: The normalized target is the generic 180-EC Economics and Business Economics bachelor. The current official curriculum has a shared 60-EC first year, three formal profiles from Year 2, a 30-EC third-year minor or study-abroad block, four 5-EC profile courses and a 10-EC thesis. The Economics profile is instantiated because it is the least specialized and most general continuation of the shared programme. For its Year 3 choice rule, the pathway takes all four named Economics profile courses rather than substituting an elective.

alternatives.label: Economics, policy & quantitative analysis
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is centred on microeconomics, macroeconomics and public policy, supported by business foundations, finance, mathematics, data science, statistics and econometrics.
alternatives.concept: The closest UCR response follows the selected Economics profile through micro- and macroeconomics, public policy, finance, mathematics, statistics, data and econometrics, while adding institutional and organisational perspectives.
progression: Economics, business, programming, research and mathematical foundations precede data modelling, advanced microeconomics, public economics, organisational analysis, probability, econometrics, behavioural economics and finance. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is offered in its assigned term.

alternatives.label: Business economics, finance & enterprise
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum combines accounting and finance with strategy, marketing, entrepreneurship, organisations, leadership, international business and empirical analysis.
alternatives.concept: This Business Economics route centres financial and organisational decisions while combining accounting, banking, strategy, marketing, entrepreneurship, leadership, international business and research.
progression: Business, economics, data, research, ethics and communication foundations precede strategy, law, marketing, international business, organisational psychology, machine learning, econometrics and finance. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is offered in its assigned term.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest route, this programme replaces mathematics, probability, public economics, EU politics and behavioural economics with strategy, leadership communication, business law, marketing, product design and entrepreneurship. Its organising focus is therefore the financial, organisational and entrepreneurial decision-making of firms.

alternatives.label: International economics, sustainability & development
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines economics, international business and econometrics with climate, sustainability governance, renewable systems, environmental justice and comparative institutions.
alternatives.concept: This route follows the programme’s International Economics and Sustainable Development direction by combining trade, growth, public policy and econometrics with climate science, sustainability governance, renewable systems, environmental justice and comparative institutions.
progression: Economics, business, research, data and sustainability foundations precede macroeconomics, machine learning, advanced microeconomics, public economics, sustainability governance, international business, econometrics and renewable-system design. Sustainability Essentials I precedes Sustainability Essentials II, which precedes Renewable System Design. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is offered in its assigned term.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest and Business Economics routes, this programme replaces much of their mathematics, organisational, marketing and enterprise work with a sequenced sustainability core, climate change, sustainability governance, renewable systems, environmental justice and comparative politics. The curricular centre is international development under ecological and institutional constraints.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target is the generic degree with three formal profiles. Economics is the least specialized and most general continuation of the shared curriculum, centred on economic theory, markets, policy and quantitative methods; the choice was made before considering UCR fit.

selection.assessment: The closest route covers the general Economics profile and its shared quantitative core. The two remaining formal generator-backed profiles, Business Economics and International Economics and Sustainable Development, both yield coherent and feasible UCR curricula with materially different course sets. Three alternatives are therefore included, which is the maximum.

blocks: Both introduce consumer and firm behaviour, markets and microeconomic reasoning.
Both develop macroeconomic analysis of growth, inflation, unemployment and policy.
Microeconomics & Behavior covers firms, market structure and strategic interaction, but in a broader behavioural curriculum.
Both examine government intervention, taxation, redistribution and public policy.
Both study observed economic behaviour and experimental evidence.
Both provide a broad introduction to economic and business organisations and their decisions.
Both develop financial accounting and interpretation of financial statements.
Both address investment and financial decision-making; UCR also covers money, banking and business planning.
Negotiation & Strategic Thinking overlaps with strategic interaction and decision-making, but is broader than the comparator’s advanced microeconomics course.
Mathematical Methods provides calculus and related quantitative foundations for economics.
Research Methods & Statistics provides statistical and empirical-research foundations.
Both develop practical data analysis and visualisation.
Both develop matrix and linear-algebra methods for quantitative analysis.
Econometrics directly develops estimation, testing, causal analysis and prediction.
Both develop structured written and oral communication for academic and professional work.
Market Research applies research design, data collection and analysis to a business question.
Groningen requires a dedicated empirical economics paper; UCR includes several research-intensive courses but no identical canonical component.
Groningen reserves 30 EC for a genuine minor, study-abroad semester or internship; the UCR alternatives are complete fixed examples.
Groningen requires a 10-EC economics thesis. UCR optional independent research is shown separately.

notes.text: Groningen provides a structured Economics profile with dedicated sequences in mathematics, macroeconomics, trade, banking and advanced economic theory, plus a 30-EC minor and a required thesis. UCR can build coherent economics, business and sustainable-development programmes, but it does not reproduce the same specialist sequence or formal profile structure.
